rachael: Quick Q manager wants to promote someone currently on a 6-month probation (joined 2 months ago). Can we do an off-cycle promo during probation?
owen: Short answer: possible but rare. Need documented exceptional contribution + manager rationale. Who signed off during hire on banding?
diego: If hire packet had a band set, changing it during probation needs Comp Ops + Sr People Ops approval and an evidence packet showing new responsibilities and impact. Also check offer terms for any guaranteed salary timelines.mina: Also tax and benefits: if title change involves comp change, verify payroll timing to avoid duplicate tax reporting periods. If promo effective retro into prior month, payroll will need a reconciliation ticket.
people-ops-bot: Leveling checklist: https://intra.redwood/people-ops/leveling-checklist. Required: impact summary, 2 concrete examples with metrics, manager endorsement, evidence of sustained performance (even during probation). Use /templates/leveling-evidence.md.
rachael: Manager says execs verbally supported it in hiring debrief. Is that enough?
owen: Verbal exec support helps but approvals must be recorded in Promo Portal/Workday. For exceptions during probation we require written exec confirmation + Comp Ops signoff.
diego: If evidence is thin manager should hand it back via portal with these bullets: 1) add 2 specific examples (metrics if possible), 2) explain how scope exceeds initial hire expectations, 3) attach written exec note if claiming exec approval. Resubmit within 10 business days.mina: Note on PIP overlap: if the IC is on a performance improvement plan, we generally hold off promos until plan is closed successfully. Promo during active PIP requires Sr People Ops + Comp Ops signoff and strong documented rationale.
rachael: Got it. I'll ask manager to build the packet and attach exec note. Thanks all :thumbsup:
